lem-base-change-of-a-zero-dimensional-pr.statement: Assume AC. For a field extension k subset K, a homogeneous ideal I in k[x_0,...,x_n], the standard graded quotient S with X=Proj S chartwise zero-dimensional, and S_K=S tensor_k K graded degreewise with X_K=Proj(S_K): S_K is standard graded with (S_K)_m=S_m tensor_k K, so dim_K(S_K)_m=dim_k S_m; the chart rings of X_K are A_i tensor_k K and X_K is chartwise zero-dimensional; and len_K(X_K)=len_k(X).
lem-base-change-of-a-zero-dimensional-pr.strategy: Identify the base-changed polynomial quotient and each graded piece by tensor algebra, then commute field extension with graded localization to obtain the charts A_i tensor_k K. Each zero-dimensional chart is finite-dimensional, so its base change remains zero-dimensional. An empty chart has A_i=0 and contributes no points; on a nonempty chart use the finite-product spectrum theorem for its local Artin factors. Compare the weighted local lengths through finite-dimensional affine consistency: each local factor B has dim_K(B tensor_k K)=dim_k B. This proves equality of total lengths even for empty X and arbitrary field extensions.

lem-eventual-hilbert-function-equals-zer.statement: Assume AC. Let I⊂k[x_0,…,x_n] be any homogeneous ideal, S=k[x_0,…,x_n]/I, and X=Proj S zero-dimensional, including the empty case. Then for all sufficiently large m, dim_k S_m=len_k(X)=Σ_x length_{O_{X,x}}(O_{X,x})[κ(x):k]. Saturation of I is not assumed.
lem-eventual-hilbert-function-equals-zer.strategy: If k is finite, pass to K=k(t), using the base-change lemma to preserve graded dimensions, chartwise dimension zero and total length. Over the resulting infinite field choose a degree-one L avoiding the finite Proj point set; for empty X take L=x_0. Then X=D_+(L)=Spec A with A=(S_L)_0. For nonempty X the finite local decomposition and nonempty finite-product spectrum theorem give finite-dimensional A and dim_k A=len_k(X); for empty X the sheaf empty-section lemma gives A=0 and the same equality. Fractions show the images of S_m→A eventually fill finite-dimensional A. Since D_+(L)=X, powers of the variables lie in LS; a pigeonhole bound gives S_m=LS_{m-1} in high degrees. The L-torsion kernels then have eventually constant dimensions and are killed by a common power of L, so they eventually vanish. Thus S_m≅A for all large m, with no saturation assumption.

ex-convolution-on-a-discrete-group.statement: Assume AC. For a discrete group G with Haar measure μ=c·counting, the L1 involution is f*(x)=overline{f(x^{-1})}, convolution is the absolutely convergent series (f*g)(x)=c∑_y f(y)g(y^{-1}x), and c^{-1}1_{ {e} } is its norm-one two-sided unit, also when G is uncountable.
ex-convolution-on-a-discrete-group.strategy: Use AC-qualified L1 convolution and density of finitely supported functions. Counting measure makes each L1 class pointwise unique and its integral a weighted sum. Prove the series is absolutely convergent and L1-bounded by finite-subsum estimates, then identify it with the L1 convolution by density. Directly compute the unit and involution from discrete unimodularity.

ex-convolution-on-a-compact-group.statement: Assume AC. With normalized Haar on compact G, 1*1=1. For finite-dimensional irreducible unitary π,σ and first-variable-linear coefficients, the convolution is zero if they are inequivalent; if T:W→V is a unitary intertwiner, it is (⟨u,Tz⟩/dim π) f^π_{Tw,v}, independent of T.
ex-convolution-on-a-compact-group.strategy: Under AC, use normalized Haar, L1/L2 density and strong continuity to identify the coefficient convolution with the pointwise integral. Form the averaged intertwiner, use irreducibility and an eigenvalue to show it is zero for inequivalent representations and scalar times any unitary intertwiner otherwise. Compute the scalar by a rank-one trace and verify independence of the intertwiner; the constant function has convolution square one.

lem-differential-of-morphism-via-cotange.statement: For an S-morphism f:X→Y, universal derivations induce df:f^*Ω_{Y/S}→Ω_{X/S}. At x over y, its cotangent fibre has source (Ω_{Y/S,y}⊗κ(y))⊗_{κ(y)}κ(x); dualising over κ(x) gives a tangent map into the dual of that extended cotangent space. Identity and composition obey the chain rule.
lem-differential-of-morphism-via-cotange.strategy: Represent the S-derivation O_Y→f_*Ω_{X/S} and adjoint to f^*. At x tensor the source stalk with κ(x), explicitly extending the cotangent space at y along κ(y)→κ(x), then dualise. Check identity and chain rule on universal differentials; composition of pullbacks follows from associativity of the sheaf tensor products defining pullback.

lem-haar-translations-are-strongly-conti.statement: Assume AC. Left translation L_gf(x)=f(g^{-1}x) is strongly continuous on L¹(G) and L²(G); the modularly corrected right translation R_gf(x)=Δ(g)^{1/2}f(xg) is strongly continuous on L²(G).
lem-haar-translations-are-strongly-conti.strategy: For f∈C_c, use the unscaled right translate ρ_gf(x)=f(xg) and the left translate from the compact-support translation lemma; near e their supports lie in one compact set and both converge uniformly. Continuity Δ(g)^{1/2}→1 then gives ||R_gf−f||∞≤Δ(g)^{1/2}||ρ_gf−f||∞+|Δ(g)^{1/2}−1|||f||∞→0 for the modular R_g. Finite Haar measure of the compact support converts uniform convergence to L1/L2 convergence. Extend by C_c density and translation isometries for arbitrary neighbourhoods and points; AC is inherited through density.

lem-gaussian-elimination-produces-a-pivo.statement: Every g in GL_n(F_q) can be written b_1 P_sigma b_2 for b_1,b_2 in B and sigma in S_n=Sym({1,...,n}); the algorithm produces a permutation matrix P_sigma by elementary triangular row and column operations.
lem-gaussian-elimination-produces-a-pivo.strategy: Work from the bottom row: choose its leftmost nonzero column, clear entries above that pivot by adding a multiple of the bottom row to an earlier row, clear entries to its right by adding a multiple of the pivot column to a later column, and scale. Delete the pivot row and column and induct on the remaining invertible block. All left and right operations lie in B; at termination exactly one nonzero entry remains in each row and column. Uniqueness of the double coset is proved in the next lemma.
lem-gaussian-elimination-produces-a-pivo.repair_kind: Statement type correction: sigma belongs to S_n, not the underlying index set; proof already constructs that permutation.
